rationale: bugs_open/394. request_render_audit selects a site's live pages ORDER BY COALESCE(nav_order,999), name and takes the first max_pages, so it takes the SAME deterministic prefix on every run. Pages past the cap are not audited less often - they have never been audited and never will be. bugs_closed/242 made this loud (a durable RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED row) and raised the cap 25->60 as a stated mitigation; the signal has no reader and the mitigation has been outgrown. MEASURED 2026-08-26: webdesign.co.uk is 146 live pages, 60 audited, 86 never - and the tail is a CLASS, not a count. Its nav_order bands are 0..90 (6 nav pages), 100 (94 tools, alphabetical), 200 (48 tool-*-guide pages), 201 (1). The cap cuts between tool-head-architect and tool-html-minifier, so all 45 remaining guide pages are unreachable at ANY cap below 98, on a site that grew 15 pages in two days. That is why the bug's candidate 3 (raise the cap) is rejected on a measurement rather than a preference - and the premise is false anyway, because max_pages is per-DISPATCH not per-agent (the 2026-08-11 '5 of 26' row carries {"max_pages":5} under render-audit-agent, resolving the bug's own [UNEXPLAINED] note). So: a keyset coverage cursor, making max_pages a per-run spend dial instead of a coverage cliff. THE DECISION THIS TURNED ON: a plain cursor takes webdesign's per-page re-measurement latency to 3 days x ceil(146/60) = ~9 days. Migration 469 is an OWNER INSTRUCTION of 2026-08-18 whose stated why is that the render audit is the only thing that GRADES a contrast repair, so its window IS the confirmation latency of the repair loop, and seven days was unacceptable. A plain cursor therefore does not merely underperform that ruling, it exceeds the condition the owner ordered removed. It dissolves rather than trades: the protected population is not the site but the pages awaiting a grade, and MEASURED 2026-08-26 with the grader's own predicate that is 3 open contrast_failure items across 3 paths on webdesign (fleet max 17 paths, on a 37-page site that never truncates at 60). So the window is a UNION - the finding-bearing pages ride every run, the cursor covers the rest - at a cost of 3 of 60 slots. Grading latency stays at 469's 3 days; coverage of the 86 invisible pages goes from never to one cycle.

plan.summary: Give request_render_audit a keyset coverage cursor (opt-in, default off) whose window is the union of an open-contrast_failure priority set and the next N-k pages from the cursor, so the capped sweep rotates instead of repeating a prefix - while preserving the 3-day repair-grading latency migration 469 was commissioned to buy. Plus the reader the owner commissioned for RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED, whose alarm conditions the cursor changes.

edits.rationale: The defect and its fix both live here. Adds one optional config key rotate_coverage (default false - the owner's 2026-08-02 rule that new authority on a shared seam ships opt-in with the unsafe side as the default; budget goes 6->7 of N=10). Selects the extra ordering columns, moves windowing into a pure helper, reads/writes the cursor, assembles the priority union, and splits the truncation message and context by mode. Prefix mode is byte-identical to today, which is what makes the two existing tests a compatibility guard rather than a rewrite.

The cursor arithmetic and the priority selection are pure functions of (rows, cursor, cap) and belong outside the dispatch action so every branch is testable without a network or a DB. The priority predicate is DERIVED from the grader rather than restated: it reuses sqlInList(workItemClosedStatuses), the same constant loadAuditRetractionCandidates interpolates, so the detector and the grader cannot drift.

The grader identifies a page by the path embedded in item_key - workItemKey("contrast_failure", path+"#"+selector) - and has never read page_id. The inverse belongs beside the composer so the pair is one edit away from staying in step; putting it in the caller would create a second notion of which page, agreeing today and diverging the first time a row is filed differently.

Every guard proven by inducing the fault, never by observing zero findings. The two cases that matter most are the ones a natural test suite omits: a priority page must NOT advance the cursor (or the pages between it and the window are never audited by anything), and the priority context keys must be present when ZERO - a key that appears only on a bad run makes its absence ambiguous between none and binary-too-old.

The cursor table and the config flip must travel together - rotate_coverage true against a missing table would fail the first cursor read - so they are one transaction. _HOLD because the discovery runner hard-fails on a capability the binary lacks, so this must be applied by hand after the image rolls; the suffix matches run-migrations.sh's SIDECAR_RE so the runner lists it and skips it. The verify block is DO/RAISE, not SELECT: ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result, so a SELECT verify cannot stop the COMMIT.

Precedent 643. Rolling back must restore today's behaviour exactly, and it does so by construction: removing the key returns rotate to its default false, and dropping the table removes state the code only reads when rotate is true. The two must be undone in that order - key first, then table - or a run between the statements would read a missing table with rotate still on.

The reader the owner commissioned (decision 4, 2026-08-25). A cursor does not discharge it: it changes what the row MEANS, so the unhealthy variants need an alarm. Cloned from ungradedcompletions.go (DBG-077 shape). It must physically contain both RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED and agent_error_log because the registry checker OPENS this file and greps it - a reader claim that cannot be satisfied by typing.

DBG-075 requires the flip in the SHIPPING commit, and the entry's own why says 'upgraded when it ships'. reader_sink is mandatory because consumed was silently ambiguous between a reader that reads the code and one that reads a different table - the field exists so an entry cannot pass the reader check while reading the wrong sink.

That is the precedent for advancing at dispatch, and the reason the cursor gets its own table rather than a column here.

request_render_audit_action.go sets neither CheckConfig nor StrictConfig on RequestRenderAuditInputSpec (verified 2026-08-26), so an old binary meeting rotate_coverage in step config ignores it silently - every image/config skew order is inert rather than wrong.

LANDMINES, footprint CheckResult.Resolved: 'A monotonic check's if len(findings) == 0 { return } early return makes its new retraction INERT on exactly the sites that need it' - the reason the zero-priority context keys are asserted PRESENT rather than omitted, and the reason the truncation row is written before the produce while the cursor is written after.
plan.risks: REGRADE LATENCY IS PRESERVED; NEW-DEFECT DETECTION LATENCY IS PARTIALLY TRADED, and the second half must not be dropped when reporting the first. Preserved: every page carrying an open contrast_failure is in every run, so repair-grading and park-draining stay at the 3-day cadence migration 469 bought, bounded only by the half-window reserve (today 3 of a 30-slot reserve on the one truncating site). Traded: detection of a NEW defect on webdesign's first-60 pages degrades from every 3 days to one cycle (~9 days at 146 pages over a 57-slot rotation), because a page with no open finding has no claim on the priority set. In exchange, detection on the 86 structurally invisible pages goes from NEVER to one cycle. That is the actual bargain - head-page detection latency spent buying tail-page coverage, on exactly one site, at one cap. If ~9 days is unacceptable there, max_pages is now a pure latency dial with no coverage cliff behind it, so raising it for that one agent shortens the cycle without reintroducing the bug. SECOND: the priority set must not starve coverage. It is bounded at max_pages/2 so the rotation always keeps at least half the window, and the over-budget drop is selected cyclically from the cursor so the dropped excess is not the same pages every run - the deterministic-prefix disease reappearing in miniature, which is exactly what this change exists to remove. The drop is logged with the paths named and stamped durably in context; a silent cap here would be the original bug rebuilt one level down. THIRD: a stalled cursor is a new silent failure mode - if the cursor stops advancing, coverage looks healthy (rows keep arriving, mode says cursor) while nothing new is measured. That is precisely alarm condition (b) in the commissioned reader, and it is why the reader is in this submission rather than deferred. FOURTH: collation. The boundary is found by exact tuple match first and only falls back to Go tuple comparison, so Go-vs-Postgres ordering could differ only for a DELETED page with a non-ASCII name; page names are ASCII slugs today and the settling query is SELECT datcollate FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database(). FIFTH: the design-critique caller is left in prefix mode deliberately. It is manual-only with no cadence (its own seed file says so), its cap of 8 is plausibly meant as the most important 8 for a vision critique rather than any 8, and silently rotating what a critique looks at would change the product without anyone deciding to. It keeps writing prefix rows, which the reader acks by name - so a NEW unacked caller pages, and this one does not. SIXTH, stated because it is a real coupling rather than a hazard: what a clean result MEANS drifts over time. Cost per run is unchanged (same page count on the dedicated pod) but a clean cursor-mode result asserts cleanliness of its window, not of the site. findings_written already stamps truncated/pages_total/pages_audited from the echoed summary so no artefact claims whole-site, and the reader is the compensating control for the human habit of reading zero-inserted as site-clean.
